messages:
Sam W.: Quick note — hit a case where a pinned variant that was supposed to be retired continued to receive traffic after the rollout. Repro and logs below. Need a clear handshake pattern for retire/soft-deprecate vs pin affinity.

Aisha: Can you paste the minimal rollout metadata that triggered it?

Sam W.: sure — root of problem looks like this in the manifest we pushed:
```json
{
  \"model_id\": \"gpt-redwood-v2\",
  \"variant\": \"f16-q4\",
  \"pin\": true,
  \"retire_at\": 1700000000,
  \"soft_deprecate\": true
}
```
Routing logs show client pinned session still routed to variant after retire_at. Client checks retire_at only at session start.

Jun K.: My hunch: lifecycle transitions are ambiguous. We have two signals (soft_deprecate boolean and retire_at timestamp) and client/runtime honor only one. Also cache/kvs still have affinity.

Toni: We discussed similar in the RFC but didn't standardize a small state machine. Proposal: introduce a compact lifecycle object so both control-plane and runtime have deterministic semantics. Example:
```json
"lifecycle": {
  "state": "active",    // active | deprecated | retiring | retired
  "transition_at": 1700000000, // when next state becomes effective
  "cache_retention_seconds": 3600,
  "client_grace_window_seconds": 300,
  "pin_override_allowed": "tenant"  // none | tenant | always
}
```
Goal: clients use state+transition to decide routing and whether to keep long-lived sessions pinned.

Aisha: Nice. Two operational questions: 1) when state==deprecated should runtime still run inference for existing pinned sessions? 2) what to do about KV cache eviction? We want to avoid a cold-surge.

Jun K.: Suggest semantics: deprecated -> continue serving existing sessions, no new sessions (unless pin_override_allowed says tenant). retiring -> start background draining: reject new sessions, start cache eviction policy but honor cache_retention_seconds for pinned sessions. retired -> stop serving; start tombstone.

Sam W.: I like that. For caches: add explicit cache_retention_seconds and per-tenant override. Also add a short-lived lease token the control plane issues to pinned sessions so runtime can validate pinned session validity even if variant moves to retiring.

Toni: We'll need to extend rollout migration tooling to go through states: active -> deprecated -> retiring -> retired. Ops needs to be able to force skip to retired in emergencies.

ops-oncall: @Toni noted — can we include an emergency flag (force_retire=true) that bypasses grace windows? Should be gated by RBAC and audit logs.

Jun K.: Yes, force_retire allowed but audited. Also ensure that RPCs between control plane and runtime exchange lifecycle state diffs atomically to avoid race.

Aisha: Implementation nit: clients currently look for retire_at numeric only. We'll add lifecycle.state check and fallback to retire_at for back-compat. Migration plan: clients >= v3 will read lifecycle; older clients will continue to use retire_at until EOL.

Sam W.: Sample + migration note to include in RFC:
```json
// back-compat: lifecycle absent -> treat retire_at as transition_at to retired
{
  "retire_at": 1700000000,
  "lifecycle": null
}
```

Toni: Ops runbook snippet: mark variants as deprecated 48h before retiring by default. retiring gets a 24h cache retention period for pinned sessions unless tenant overrides. Emergency retire can be called but requires two-person approval.

Aisha: Edge case: what if tenant pins a variant with pin_override_allowed==tenant and then we retire it? Tenant expectation may be that their pin survives — need clear SLA on how long pins survive after retirement. Recommend default: tenant pins survive through retiring + cache_retention_seconds but not into retired. If tenant needs longer, they must migrate to a new pinned variant.

Sam W.: Decision summary (agreed): 1) Add lifecycle object with state enum and transition_at. 2) Add cache_retention_seconds and client_grace_window_seconds. 3) Add pin_override_allowed with tenant-level semantics. 4) Support force_retire with RBAC/audit. 5) Back-compat: retire_at continues to be honored as transition_at when lifecycle missing.

Jun K.: Action items: - @Toni to update schema and draft RFC patch; - @ops-oncall to prepare migration runbook and emergency retire play; - @Infra-bot to schedule a rolling conversion job marking existing variants as deprecated->retiring with default windows.

Toni: I'll open the RFC patch today and include the sample schemas and runbook.

Infra-bot: rollout/cleanup job queued for 2026-04-15T02:00Z :eyes:

ops-oncall: Scheduling runbook review Wednesday. :thumbsup:
